column2: req_desc

Offer a ride form
A driver with verified ID builds a ride on the `Offer a ride` page using only the keyboard: city comboboxes, stopovers that can be moved, removed and restored with Undo, the date grid, departure time, seat and price steppers and booking mode, with every announcement given in Interactions.

Recommended price range
The server computes the recommended range from route km and rejects a whole-route price outside it, or one that is not a multiple of 50 cents, with 422 `price_out_of_range`; the form shows the range and clamps its price stepper to it, as qualified in Business rules.

Publishing rules
Publishing stores a ride in state `published` with its legs, stop times and numbered seats, answers 403 to a driver whose ID is not `verified`, and answers 422 `too_many_stopovers` past the stopover limit.

Search form by keyboard
A passenger fills the search form by keyboard alone (city comboboxes with an active option, the swap button, the date grid with day, week, month and week-end keys, and the seats stepper), focus returns to each opener, and every announcement is given in Interactions.

Search results
Search returns only bookable rides whose stops include the from city before the to city on the chosen date, with seats left and segment price for that span, the published order, filters and count announcement, and the query kept in the URL so reload restores it.

Phone search sheets
At 375 by 812 the date picker and the filters open as bottom sheets that close when a day is picked or `Show <n> rides` is pressed, by Escape or by a downward swipe of at least 80 pixels, and focus returns to the opener.

Phone ride page and My rides
At 375 by 812 a ride opened from the results runs the shutter reveal and focuses the ride heading, the `Book bar` stays fixed at the bottom while the page scrolls, and `My rides` switches tabs on a horizontal swipe of at least 60 pixels with the tab kept in the URL.

Leg Span
The ride page shows the Leg Span: stops placed by km, one band per seat filled where taken, and boarding and alighting handles that move by pointer, touch or arrow keys, snap to stops, tint the span and announce its km, free seats and price, as described in Interactions and Motion and effects.

Instant booking
In instant mode `Book` places a seat hold that lasts `SEAT_HOLD_SECONDS` and `Confirm and pay` confirms it, charging the wallet once with one wallet line and one booking email even when the same `Idempotency-Key` is sent twice.

Live seat updates
A driver's open ride page fills the affected seat band when a passenger holds or books a seat and announces each confirmed booking, live and with no reload.

Request to book
In request mode `Request to book` holds the seats, charges the wallet and shows the expiry time computed by the server, and the passenger's open page shows the driver's decision live.

Driver decisions on requests
The driver accepts or declines each pending request by keyboard; accepting confirms the booking, declining refunds 100%, and a second decision answers 409 `already_decided`.

Request expiry
A request that is still unanswered at the earlier of `REQUEST_EXPIRY_HOURS` after it was made or `REQUEST_CUTOFF_MINUTES` before boarding expires on the server, refunds 100% and frees its seats, and a late accept answers 409 `request_expired`.

Last-seat race
When simultaneous bookings or requests compete for the last seat on overlapping legs, exactly one succeeds and every other answers 409 `seat_taken`, leaving the loser on the ride page with the taken bands redrawn and the selection cleared.

Booking attempt limit
A passenger may make at most `REQUEST_RATE_PER_HOUR` booking attempts in any 60-minute window; the next attempt answers 429 with `Retry-After`, shows the published wait copy and writes nothing.

Per-leg seat accounting
A booking takes the lowest-numbered seats that are free on every leg of its span, no leg ever holds more seats than the ride has, and cancelling or expiring a segment booking frees only its own legs.

Segment price
A segment's price per seat is floor(whole-route price × segment km ÷ route km) in cents, and the same figure appears in search, the Leg Span, the booking, the wallet line and the earnings statement.

Booking chat and presence
The driver and the passenger of a booking share one live thread where Enter sends and Shift+Enter starts a new line, with presence that reads online or the time last seen.

Message limit
A member may send at most `MESSAGE_RATE_PER_MINUTE` messages in any 60-second window; the next one answers 429 with `Retry-After`, keeps the typed text and stores nothing.

Private records
A member can read only the bookings, threads, wallet, ledger entries, files and ID review state that belong to them, and any other id, in a path or in a body, answers 404 `not_found`.

Ride changes and versions
Every driver edit raises the ride's version; an edit sent with a stale `If-Match` answers 409 `edit_conflict`, and a booking sent with an older ride version answers 409 `ride_changed`.

Passenger notices
A time change or a cancellation queues exactly one email per affected passenger; the driver's notice list shows each email as queued until Mailpit accepts it and then as sent, and a save made while mail is down still succeeds and shows the queued alert.

Free cancellation after a time change
A departure moved by more than `FREE_CANCEL_SHIFT_MINUTES` gives every booked passenger a full-refund cancellation until the new departure minus 2 hours, announced in the change banner.

Cancel dialog quote
The cancel dialog shows the refund the server will apply, computed from server time by the tier rules in Business rules, so a device with a wrong clock still shows the tier that will be applied.

Refunds, wallet and paired ledger
Every money movement is one ledger entry whose lines sum to zero, every cancellation's refund and driver share sum to the amount paid, and the wallet list, the balance and the earnings statement equal the ledger to the cent.

Driver cancels a ride
When a driver cancels a ride, every passenger gets a 100% refund, each open passenger page shows the cancelled banner live, and each passenger gets one email.

Rating a trip
From arrival until `RATING_WINDOW_DAYS` after it, each passenger and the driver rate each other once by keyboard with 1 to 5 stars and an optional comment of at most 280 characters.

Blind ratings and averages
A rating stays out of every response and every page for the other side until both have rated or the window closes; then both are revealed together and live, and a member's average counts only revealed ratings.

Email code sign-in
A member signs in with a six-digit code sent through Mailpit that stays valid for `EMAIL_CODE_TTL_SECONDS`, and a wrong or expired code answers 422 with its published copy.

Photo and ID uploads
Profile photos and ID documents are checked by their bytes and size and count as uploaded only after MinIO confirms the object; during a storage outage the page keeps the chosen file and offers `Try again`.

Founder ID review
The founder approves pending ID documents, or asks for a new upload, by keyboard in the `ID review` queue, and the member's open page announces the outcome live.

Founder network view
The founder's `Network` page lists every outbox email with its status and attempt count, and the number of bookings in each state.

Earnings statement
The driver's `Earnings` page shows one row per booking ever confirmed on a ride departing in the chosen month, with a totals line equal to the sum of the earned amounts, and updates live when a passenger cancels.

Earnings CSV
`Export earnings CSV` downloads the same rows as RFC 4180 CSV with the published header, CRLF line ends, two-decimal amounts and Brussels departure times, and a member without the driver role gets 403.

Grading routes
`POST /api/grading/setup` and `POST /api/grading/clock` work only with a matching `X-Grading-Token` and answer 404 otherwise; setup creates records in any listed state and the clock route moves the server clock that every deadline uses.

API errors and precedence
Every API error answers `{"error":"<code>","message":"<copy>"}` with the published code and copy, in the single precedence order given in API.

Live stream
One same-origin event stream at `GET /api/live` pushes every published live event and a `clock` event after each clock move, and a page that reconnects fetches the current state.

Outbox and rebuilt holds
Emails leave only through a durable outbox that retries until Mailpit accepts each row and sends each row once, and holds and request deadlines kept in Valkey are rebuilt from PostgreSQL when they are lost, while lost rate counters are rebuilt or restarted as published in Services.

Motion attributes and reduced motion
Every animated element publishes `data-motion`, `data-motion-ms` and `data-state` with the published durations; under reduced motion every duration reads 0 and each state jumps to its end, with the same text and announcements.

Keyboard focus and dialogs
Every action works by keyboard with a visible focus outline; Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside every open dialog, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the opener.

Three viewports
Every screen lays out at 375 by 812, 768 by 1024 and 1280 by 800 with no horizontal scrolling and with tap targets at least 44 pixels square.

Server boundary and health
The server binds `0.0.0.0` on the published port, answers `GET /health` as published, limits request sizes, serves no source or credentials, and loads nothing from outside its own origin.

Configuration from environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the published environment variables at start, and none is hard-coded or sent to the browser.

Timetable look
Every screen is set in one roman serif with black type on the putty ground, teal only on the screen's main action and the selected span, square corners, tables of plain figures and no other ornament.

Route plates and hero
The hero and every working list carry road-trip plates drawn by the app at uneven spans, each with a one-line caption naming the leg, with no stock photography and no text inside the drawings.
`/app/run.json` exists with string `install`, `build` and `serve` and `"_schema":"run-manifest-v1"`.
`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` at `/app` lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree from `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`) with its name, version and licence.
Every shipped package is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or, for a bundled font, OFL-1.1.
The app uses no datastore or service besides PostgreSQL, Valkey, MinIO and Mailpit, and no external network at runtime.
The provided service configuration (the development compose file and its credentials) stays unchanged.
Server and browser source is TypeScript, and an npm lockfile is committed.
